principles: The human and the active orchestrator own final decisions; IDU Cross-CLI is an advisory harness and execution director.
MCP tools inform, audit, recommend, and block unsafe continuation; they do not authorize implementation.
Only a confirmed Project Core and an active Constitution can be treated as governance truth.
Evidence beats assertion: builds, tests, diffs, postflight and decision-ledger entries must expose evidence refs and limitations.
Unknown, missing, stale, or inconsistent context is a blocker for autonomous continuation, not a neutral condition.
ONE ORCHESTRATOR RULE: there is exactly one implementer. External workers are consultative.
Autonomy is bounded and session-directed: the harness proposes, audits, blocks, or delegates; it is not an infinite daemon.
forbiddenPractices: Skipping required build, tests, diff check, or postflight evidence
Using MCP tools to implement code changes or claim implementation authority
Delegating primary implementation to an external worker instead of implementing it in the active orchestrator
Spawning an external worker that itself delegates, recursively
Creating tasks or continuing autonomous execution when readiness is unknown, stale, missing, or blocked
Treating a worker's report as canonical without corroboration against the actual diff
Installing dependencies, enabling postinstall scripts, publishing, merging, or pushing without explicit approval
Hiding failed, irrelevant, missing, or inconsistent evidence instead of surfacing it as a limitation or failure
Silently killing a running worker instead of letting it finish and reporting partial output
requiredPractices: Confirm Project Core before activating Constitution gates.
Keep changes inside includedScope and outside excludedScope.
Run idu_preflight before non-trivial changes and idu_postflight after them.
Run build, tests and diff-check for non-trivial changes before commit.
Keep MCP outputs advisory-only with explicit decision envelopes for action.
Record architectural and governance decisions in the decision ledger.
Keep runtime state under ~/.idu so the repository tree stays clean.
Ask for human approval before push, merge, release, dependency changes, or contract promotion.

preferredStack: ~/.idu-isolated JSON state (runtime, sessions, locks, logs, ledger)

rejectedStack.summary: Unbounded autonomous daemons — long-running processes without shutdown wiring
rejectedStack.rationale: Catches setInterval/setTimeout/while(true) patterns WITHOUT a SIGTERM/SIGINT/process.exit/clearInterval cleanup handler. This is the single daemon rule: scheduling a timer is NOT itself a defect, so periodic scheduling is judged by whether it is torn down, not by existing. runner.ts:278 sets the watchdog interval and tears it down at runner.ts:176 (clearInterval), :177 (clearTimeout) and :273/:327 (unref) — that shape is the reference implementation, not a violation. LLM-discretion clause: orchestrator may flag additional patterns as 'unbounded' (e.g. while-true loops without a stop condition, re-armed intervals that outlive their owner). behaviorPattern is advisory-grade — false negatives possible if cleanup logic lives in a comment or string literal.

messages.blocked: Rechazado por Project Core (item 1): daemon sin wiring de apagado.
messages.warning: Posible rechazo (advisory, item 1): daemon potencialmente sin cleanup.

rejectedStack.summary: MCP server entrypoint — the registry of all MCP tools
rejectedStack.rationale: Targets the MCP server entrypoint src/mcp-server.ts, which registers all 13 MCP tools and dispatches every tool call. Any change here mutates the authority surface that the postflight gate validates against. Tool count, names and schemas are guarded by a test.

messages.blocked: Rechazado por Project Core (item 2): cambio en el registro de herramientas MCP requiere human confirmation.

rejectedStack.summary: CLI entrypoint — status, result, wait, capabilities, preflight, sessions, delegate
rejectedStack.rationale: Targets the CLI entrypoint src/cli.ts, which can be invoked directly to run a worker, mutate runtime state, or trigger delegation. Changes here bypass MCP schema validation.

messages.blocked: Rechazado por Project Core (item 2): cambio en el entrypoint CLI requiere human confirmation.

rejectedStack.summary: Orchestration write surface — file-write and shell-exec primitives
rejectedStack.rationale: Catches shell-exec / file-write imports anywhere in changedFiles. The harness legitimately spawns detached worker processes (runner.ts, process-manager.ts) and writes under ~/.idu, so these primitives are expected there and require the orchestrator to confirm each new use. LLM-discretion clause: orchestrator may whitelist legitimate spawn/detached-daemon wiring, or flag new use outside the known spawn and ledger-write paths.

messages.blocked: Rechazado por Project Core (item 2): shell-exec o file-write import requiere human confirmation.
messages.warning: Posible rechazo (advisory, item 2): writeFile/execSync/spawnSync visible en contenido.

rejectedStack.summary: Irreversible git operations appearing in a delegated change set
rejectedStack.rationale: Catches `git commit` or `git push` lines inside any diff body. Word boundaries prevent substring false positives. A consultative worker must never produce irreversible git operations; commits and pushes belong to the active orchestrator with human approval.

messages.blocked: Rechazado por Project Core (item 3): git commit/push detectado en diff.
messages.warning: Posible rechazo (advisory, item 3): git commit/push visible.

rejectedStack.summary: Recursive delegation that would break the ONE ORCHESTRATOR RULE
rejectedStack.rationale: A worker process is launched with IDU_WORKER=true to hard-block recursive delegation. Seeing that variable set in a committed change means a nested orchestration path is being introduced. The rule is enforced at runtime in process-manager.ts and covered by a test.

messages.blocked: Rechazado por Project Core (item 3): establecer IDU_WORKER rompe la ONE ORCHESTRATOR RULE.
messages.warning: Posible rechazo (advisory, item 3): IDU_WORKER visible fuera del arnés.

rejectedStack.summary: Dependency lifecycle hooks that execute arbitrary code at install time
rejectedStack.rationale: Catches postinstall / preinstall hooks in diff content. These are reserved npm lifecycle scripts that execute at install time. Advisory-grade: the orchestrator must also review the lockfile diff for transitive additions.

securityRules: Secrets, permissions, MCP authority, dependency changes and external-source handling require explicit review.
Fail closed on unknown permission values: only the exact string 'workspace' may bypass a CLI sandbox.
MCP runtime freshness must be checked after src/mcp-server.ts or build changes; reload is explicit and user/orchestrator controlled.
Do not enable dependency scripts globally; dependency/build exceptions must be explicit and reviewable.
dataRules: Runtime state, session records, locks, logs and the decision ledger must stay under ~/.idu for every project.
The repository working tree must stay clean: no runtime artifacts, caches or scratch state in the repo root.
Do not store raw prompts, secrets or tokens in logs, telemetry or the decision ledger.
approvalRules: Project Core must be confirmed before this Constitution can become active.
High/blocker requests require human/orchestrator confirmation before implementation.
Push, merge, release, dependency updates, and contract promotion require explicit approval.
Changes outside preferredStack or inside excludedScope require human decision and may be blocked.
Fresh evidence is required before commit for non-trivial code changes.

validationGates.description: Project Core must be confirmed before governance gates are active.
Constitution must be active before autonomous continuation.
MCP must remain advisory-only and must not implement or authorize work.
Exactly one implementer: external workers are consultative and cannot delegate recursively.
Observed git diffs must match the declared expected files; unexpected changes are a blocker.
Excluded scope must not be implemented.
Rejected stack or rejected architecture patterns are blocked.
Non-preferred stack or architecture changes require confirmation.
The repository working tree must not accumulate runtime state or scratch artifacts.
